title: Prediction of Listener Perception of Argumentative Speech in a Crowdsourced Dataset Using (Psycho-)Linguistic and Fluency Features
reasoning: The paper focuses on predicting human perception of argumentative speech based on linguistic and fluency features. While the topics for the speeches (e.g., mandatory vaccination, AI development) have ethical dimensions, the paper itself does not analyze, evaluate, or benchmark ethics, morals, or faith. The analysis is centered on communicative effectiveness and listener perception (e.g., 'persuasive', 'informative', 'confusing').
